summary: Assen's eight public car parks (seven in the inner city, one in Kloosterveen) are owned by the municipality, and the 2026 parking tax ordinance sets a uniform garage tariff of 0.50 euro per 15 minutes with an 8 euro daily maximum, unchanged from 2025 (the maximum was 7.50 euros with evening caps of 3 euros in 2023), while on-street meters charge 0.50 euro per 12 minutes. Paid parking covers the inner city and zones 1-9 around it, with 120-minute limits on most centre streets, and a zero-emission zone for delivery vehicles has applied in the pedestrian core since January 2025. The July 2025 Visie mobiliteit 2040 states that about 450 garage spaces stay unused on peak Saturday afternoons and that fewer than half of more than 800 on-street centre spaces are occupied, and it announces a parking strategy, phased extension of regulated parking, a parking ring leading to garages and a station mobility hub, though in January 2026 the parking strategy was still listed as an open commitment. The P+R Stationsplein (266 spaces) is operated by Q-Park; the municipality is also planning collective garages for the Havenkwartier, has received a permit application to rebuild the Doevenkamp garage, and is expanding EV charging under its Laadvisie 2023-2027. The municipal website was offline on 21 October 2026, so current municipal pages could not be read.

items.text: Assen's council adopted the Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026 on 18 December 2025, in force with levy from 1 January 2026. Its tariff table sets 0.50 euro per 12 minutes (2.50 euros per hour) at on-street meters and 0.30 euro per 10 minutes with a 6 euro daily maximum at Veemarktplein and part of Industrieweg; the table lists the same amounts for 2025 and 2026.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Assen)

items.text: For all municipal car parks the 2026 tariff table sets 0.50 euro per 15 minutes (2.00 euros per hour) and an 8 euro daily maximum that applies only to consecutive hours within one day. Monthly garage passes are 37.50 euros for Assen residents, 68.50 euros for a 7x24 worker pass and 80 euros for a 7x24 pass for non-residents.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Assen)

items.text: Street resident permits where meters apply cost 15.48 euros per month or 180.60 euros per year, and a worker permit (5x24, by plate) costs 36.12 euros per month. The fine-related naheffingsaanslag costs 82 euros plus one hour of the local tariff, and the council budgeted about 4,000 of them for 2026.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (Assen)

items.text: Under the Aanwijzingsbesluit parkeren (version in force from 19 December 2025), paid parking in zones 1-8 runs Monday-Saturday 9:00-21:00 and Sunday 12:00-18:00, with a 120-minute limit for paid visitors; zone 9 (Assen Oost) is paid Monday-Friday 9:00-18:00. In the inner city paid parking runs 9:00-18:00 Monday-Saturday (Friday until 21:00), Veemarktplein allows 24 hours at a time and De Stelling, Oude Molenstraat car park, Zuidersingel and Zuidhaege allow 240 minutes.

The same decision caps on-street stays at 120 minutes in inner-city streets including Stationsstraat, Groningerstraat, Mercuriusplein, Torenlaan, Brinkstraat and Weiersstraat. Parking zones 1-8 cover the ring of neighbourhoods around the centre (Vaart, Kanaal, Beilerstraat, Doevenkamp, Veemarkt areas) and zone 9 covers Assen Oost near the station.

In the 2023 ordinance garages cost 0.50 euro per 14 minutes with a 7.50 euro daily maximum, plus an evening cap of 3 euros (5 euros in De Nieuwe Kolk) for the garages Mercuriusplein, Stadhuis, Drents Museum, Neptunus, Triade and Citadel. The 2024 table lists 0.50 euro per 15 minutes and an 8 euro daily maximum and contains no evening caps, and the same 8 euro maximum is in the 2025 and 2026 tables.

Assen published its Visie mobiliteit 2040 in the Gemeenteblad on 17 July 2025. It says the centre should become a destination with the ring road turned into a 'parking ring' leading to garages, and announces a Parkeerstrategie with area-based parking plans because of rising parking nuisance and housing growth (e.g. Stadskwartier). It also proposes a phased extension of regulated parking where pressure is high, simpler rules than today's patchwork of regimes, and at least one parking survey per year; these are policy intentions, not decisions on specific zones.
items.source_title: Assen toekomstgericht op weg: Visie mobiliteit 2040 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 314762)

items.text: The Visie mobiliteit 2040 states, citing the municipal parking monitor, that on Saturday afternoon (the peak) about 450 garage spaces in the centre stay unused, and that of more than 800 on-street spaces in the centre fewer than 400 are occupied. The council therefore plans to repurpose some on-street spaces for bicycles, greenery and seating.
items.source_title: Assen toekomstgericht op weg: Visie mobiliteit 2040 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 314762)

items.text: The vision says the station could become the main mobility hub of Drenthe and names hubs at Kloosterveen, Assen-Zuid (longer term) and an upgrade of bus station Marsdijk, combining bus stops, covered bike storage, EV charging spaces, shared cars and bikes. It also states that car-parking space remains needed because the region is car-dependent, and that grid capacity limits fast-charging roll-out.
items.source_title: Assen toekomstgericht op weg: Visie mobiliteit 2040 (Gemeenteblad 2025, 314762)

items.text: A zero-emission zone for delivery vans and lorries has applied in Assen's pedestrian and window-time inner city (Markt, Brink, Oudestraat, Mercuriusplein and others) since 1 January 2025, enforced by ANPR cameras. A decision published 16 June 2026 only replaces the traffic signs with the new model signs and changes no rule.
items.source_title: Verkeersbesluit wijziging verkeersborden zero-emissiezone Binnenstad Assen (Gemeenteblad 2026, 279181)

items.text: On 26 June 2026 the municipality designated two parking spaces near Vaart N.Z. 76 for EV charging only, referring to its Laadvisie 2023-2027. The decision adds that the second space applies only once usage exceeds 4,500 kWh, with charging points placed so a network has a maximum walking distance of 250 metres.
items.source_title: Verkeersbesluit laadplaats voor elektrische auto's, Vaart N.Z. 76, Assen (Gemeenteblad 2026, 309053)

items.text: On 18 December 2025 the municipality published that it had received, on 16 December 2025, an application for an omgevingsvergunning to rebuild the car park at Doevenkamp 3. The notice gives no details of the works and says a decision is expected within eight weeks.
items.source_title: Aanvraag omgevingsvergunning, verbouwen parkeergarage Doevenkamp 3, Assen (Gemeenteblad 2025, 554772)

items.text: Q-Park lists P+R Stationsplein (Stationsplein, 9404 RT Assen) as its only car park in Assen: 266 spaces, 2.10 m height limit, open 24/7 with number plate recognition, bike parking and public transport nearby, and no tariffs shown online. The page was read on 21 October 2026.

Assen's Laadvisie 2023-2027 (version 1, February 2023) states that the municipality owns the 8 public car parks, 7 in the inner city and 1 in Kloosterveen. It also says charging points in garages fall outside the provincial charging concession and a pilot was started in four central garages (Stadhuis, De Nieuwe Kolk, Cite and Mercurius).

The Laadvisie 2023-2027 calculates about 1,000 electric cars in Assen in 2021, about 3,800 in 2025 and about 9,000 in 2030, with a computed need of 52, 190 and 465 public charge points. It aims for a covering network with a 250 m mesh in the 2023-2027 concession period and cites the national ambition of 5 percent of garage spaces with a charge point in 2025 and 10 percent in 2030.

The Sweco parking survey of April 2019 for the municipality interviewed 1,809 visitors in the 7 car parks and at street locations. Of visitors parking outside the garages, 41 percent used Mercuriusplein, 10 percent Veemarktterrein and 9 percent the P+R site at the NS station; this is a 2019 survey and may no longer reflect current use.

The Havenkwartier structuurvisie (council proposal sent 15 April 2024 for the 23 May 2024 council meeting) plans a low-car district near the station with one space per dwelling, resident parking concentrated in collective garages in building fields II and III, and a parking fund to which all developments contribute. It belongs to the Stadskwartier housing programme backed by 4.2 million euros of national housing-impulse funding.

The council's list of open commitments dated 16 January 2026 shows two parking items still open: the alderman's February 2025 promise to develop a parking strategy and a promised parking vision for the Havenkwartier, both referring to a college letter of 9 January 2026 which we could not read.

gaps: www.assen.nl returned HTTP 429 'temporarily offline' (security vulnerability notice) on 21 October 2026, so municipal parking, permit, garage and P+R pages (e.g. https://www.assen.nl/parkeren and https://www.assen.nl/locaties-en-tarieven) could not be read.

P+R Stationsplein tariffs and traveller (NS) discount: Q-Park shows 'no tariffs available online'; only commercial listing portals gave figures, which were not used. Station P+R ownership and the NS role not confirmed from a primary source.

Individual garage capacities and operator arrangements (Citadel, Mercurius, Triade, Nieuwe Kolk, Neptunus, Drents Museum, Stadhuis/Doevenkamp, Kloosterveste) could only be sourced from commercial portals, which were not used; the Laadvisie only confirms municipal ownership.

The college letter of 9 January 2026 on the Parkeerstrategie and Havenkwartier parking vision, the parkeermonitor data behind the 450 unused spaces, and the outcome of the Doevenkamp 3 permit application were not found.
No news article (RTV Drenthe, Dagblad van het Noorden) on garages, tariffs or parking policy was opened; no 2026 utilisation statement beyond the 2025 mobility vision was found.
The 2019 college proposal 'Taakstelling parkeerexploitatie & herijking parkeerbeleid' and the 2021 Binnenstadvisie were not opened.
